text: Working with APIs allows programs to communicate with each other over the internet. When you make an API request, you typically send an HTTP request using methods like GET to retrieve data or POST to send new information. The response often comes back in JSON format, which is easy for computers to read and process. Many APIs require authentication, usually through an API key, to ensure only authorised users can access the data. It is important to be aware of rate limits, as some APIs restrict the number of requests you can make per hour. Finally, always include proper error handling in your code to manage failed requests or unexpected responses gracefully.
